sanskrit: ghṛtaṃ prokṣantī subhagā devān devī gamiṣyati | paktāram aghnye mā hiṃsīr divaṃ prehi śataudane ||
english: She the auspicious one, sprinkling ghee, shall go as a goddess to the gods. O inviolable cow, do not injure the one who cooks thee; ascend to heaven, O thou of a hundred offerings.

sanskrit: ye pitaro diviṣado 'ntarikṣasadaś ca ye ceme bhūmyām adhi | tebhyas tvaṃ dhukṣva sarvadā kṣīraṃ sarpir atho madhu ||
english: Those Fathers who dwell in heaven, and those who abide in the atmosphere, and those here upon the earth — for them do thou yield at all times milk, and ghee, and honey.

sanskrit: yat te śiro ye ca śṛṅge yau karṇau yau ca te akṣyau | āmikṣāṃ duhratāṃ dātre kṣīraṃ sarpir atho madhu ||
english: Whatever is thy head, thy two horns, thy two ears, and thy two eyes — from these let the ones who milk thee yield to the giver curdled milk, ghee, and honey.

sanskrit: yat te mukhaṃ yā jihvā ye dantā ye ca te hanū | (…) ||
english: Whatever is thy mouth, thy tongue, thy teeth, and thy two jaws — [yield to the giver curdled milk, ghee, and honey].

sanskrit: yat te klomā yad dhṛdayaṃ purītat sahakaṇṭhikā | (…) ||
english: Whatever is thy lung, thy heart, thy entrails together with the throat — [yield to the giver curdled milk, ghee, and honey].

sanskrit: yat te yakṛd ye matasne āntrāṇi yāś ca te gudāḥ | (…) ||
english: Whatever is thy liver, thy kidneys, thy intestines, and thy lower bowels — [yield to the giver curdled milk, ghee, and honey].

sanskrit: yas te plāśir yo vaniṣṭur yau kukṣī yac ca ta udaram | (…) ||
english: Whatever is thy spleen, thy lower belly, thy two flanks, and thy abdomen — [yield to the giver curdled milk, ghee, and honey].

sanskrit: yas te majjā yāny asthīni yan māṃsaṃ yac ca lohitam | (…) ||
english: Whatever is thy marrow, thy bones, thy flesh, and thy blood — [yield to the giver curdled milk, ghee, and honey].

sanskrit: yau te bāhū yau te aṃsau doṣaṇī yā ca te kakut | (…) ||
english: Whatever are thy two forelegs, thy two shoulders, thy two forearms, and thy hump — [yield to the giver curdled milk, ghee, and honey].

sanskrit: ye te skandhā yā grīvā yāḥ pṛṣṭīr yāś ca parśavaḥ | (…) ||
english: Whatever are thy shoulder-blades, thy neck, thy ribs, and thy side-bones — [yield to the giver curdled milk, ghee, and honey].

sanskrit: yau ta ūrū aṣṭhīvantau ye śroṇī yā ca te bhasat | (…) ||
english: Whatever are thy two thighs, thy two knee-joints, thy two haunches, and thy hindquarters — [yield to the giver curdled milk, ghee, and honey].

sanskrit: yat te pucchaṃ ye te bālā yad ūdho ye ca te stanāḥ | (…) ||
english: Whatever is thy tail, thy tail-hairs, thy udder, and thy teats — [yield to the giver curdled milk, ghee, and honey].

sanskrit: yās te jaṅghā yāḥ kuṣṭhikā ṛtsarā ye ca te śaphāḥ | (…) ||
english: Whatever are thy shanks, thy pasterns, thy fetlock-joints, and thy hooves — [yield to the giver curdled milk, ghee, and honey].

sanskrit: yat te carma śataudane yāni lomāny aghnye | āmikṣāṃ duhratāṃ dātre kṣīraṃ sarpir atho madhu ||
english: Whatever is thy skin, O thou of a hundred offerings, whatever are thy hairs, O inviolable one — from these let those who milk thee yield to the giver curdled milk, ghee, and honey.

sanskrit: ayaṃ te stana āmikṣām ayaṃ sarpir ayaṃ madhu | ayaṃ te sarvān kāmān duhāṃ devi śataudane ||
english: This teat of thine yields curdled milk, this one ghee, this one honey. May this teat of thine, O goddess, O thou of a hundred offerings, milk forth all desires.

sanskrit: kroḍau te stāṃ puroḍāśāv ājyenābhighāritau | tau pakṣau devi kṛtvā sā dātāraṃ divaṃ vaha ||
english: May thy two flanks become the two sacrificial rice-cakes sprinkled over with ghee. Making those thy wings, O goddess, carry the giver to heaven.

sanskrit: ulūkhale musale ye ca carmaṇi ye vā śūrpe taṇḍulāḥ kaṇāḥ | yad vā vāto mātariśvā mamātha- -agniṣ ṭad dhotā suhutaṃ kṛṇotu ||
english: Whatever grains and husks are in the mortar, in the pestle, in the hide, or in the winnowing fan — whatever Mātariśvan the wind has churned, may Agni the purifier make that a well-offered oblation.

sanskrit: apo devīr madhumatīr ghṛtaścuto brahmaṇāṃ hasteṣu prapṛthak sādayāmi | yatkāma idam abhiṣiñcāmi vo 'haṃ tan no astu vayaṃ syāma patayo rayīṇām ||
english: The divine waters, sweet-flowing and dripping with ghee, I place severally into the hands of the Brāhmaṇas. With whatever desire I now sprinkle you, may that be granted to us; may we become lords of riches.

sanskrit: prajāpatiś ca parameṣṭhī ca śṛṅge indraḥ śiro agnir lalāṭaṃ yamaḥ kṛkāṭaṃ somo rājā mastiṣkaḥ | satyaṃ cakṣur ṛtaṃ śrotre prāṇāpānau nāsike dyaur uttarā hanuḥ pṛthivy adharā ||
english: Prajāpati and Parameṣṭhin are the two horns; Indra is the head; Agni is the brow; Yama is the nape of the neck; King Soma is the brain. Truth is the right eye; Ṛta is the left ear; Prāṇa and Apāna are the two nostrils; Heaven is the upper jaw; Earth is the lower jaw.

sanskrit: agnir āsyaṃ vidyuj jihvā maruto dantāḥ pavamānaḥ prāṇaḥ | viśvaṃ vāyuḥ kaṇṭhaḥ svargo lokaḥ kṛṣṇadraṃ vidharaṇī vikeśyaḥ ||
english: Agni is the mouth; lightning is the tongue; the Maruts are the teeth; Pavamāna is the breath. The All is the throat of Vāyu; the heavenly world is Kṛṣṇadra; Vidharaṇī and Vikeśī are [its parts].

sanskrit: revatī grīvāḥ kṛttikā skandhā gharmo vahaḥ śyenaḥ kroḍo antarikṣaṃ pājasyam | mitraś ca varuṇaś cāṃsau tvaṣṭā cāryamā ca doṣaṇī ||
english: The Revatī stars are the neck; the Kṛttikā stars are the shoulders; the Gharma is the back-carrier; the hawk is the chest; the atmosphere is the Pājasya. Mitra and Varuṇa are the two shoulder-joints; Tvaṣṭṛ and Aryaman are the two forearms.

sanskrit: mahādevo bāhū bṛhaspatiḥ kakud bṛhatīḥ kīkasāḥ | devānāṃ patnīḥ pṛṣṭaya upasadaḥ parśavaḥ ||
english: Mahādeva is the two forelegs; Bṛhaspati is the hump; the Bṛhatī metres are the spine-bones. The wives of the gods are the back-ridges; the Upasad rites are the ribs.

sanskrit: indrāṇī bhasad vātaḥ pucchaṃ pavamāno bālāḥ | brahma ca kṣatraṃ ca śroṇī balam ūrū dhātā ca savitā cāṣṭhīvantau ||
english: Indrāṇī is the hindquarters; Vāta is the tail; Pavamāna is the tail-hairs. Brahman and Kṣatra are the two haunches; Strength is the two thighs; Dhātṛ and Savitṛ are the two knee-joints.

sanskrit: jaṅghā gandharvā apsarasaḥ kuṣṭhikā aditiḥ śaphāḥ | ceto hṛdayaṃ yakṛn medhā harimā pittaṃ vrataṃ purītat ||
english: The Gandharvas and the Apsarases are the shanks; Aditi is the pasterns; the hooves are [hers]. The mind is the heart; the liver is wisdom; jaundice is the bile; the sacred vow is the entrails.

sanskrit: kṣut kukṣir irā vaniṣṭhuḥ parvatāḥ plāśir devajanā gudā manuṣyā āntrāṇy atrā udaram itarajanā ūbadhyaṃ rakṣāṃsi lohitam | krodho vṛkkau manyur āṇḍau prajā śepaḥ ||
english: Hunger is the flank; Irā is the lower belly; mountains are the spleen; divine beings are the lower bowels; humans are the intestines; the other beings are the contents of the stomach; Rakṣases are the blood. Anger is the two kidneys; fury is the two testicles; progeny is the phallus.

sanskrit: samudro vastir nadī sūtrī stanayitnur ūdho varṣasya pataya stanāḥ | viśvavyacāś carmauṣadhayo lomāni nakṣatrāṇi rūpam ||
english: The ocean is the bladder; the river is the urinary canal; thunder is the udder; the lords of rain are the teats. All-pervading space is the hide; plants are the body-hairs; the lunar asterisms are the form.

sanskrit: abhraṃ pīvo majjā nidhanam | nidhanaṃ bhūtyāḥ prajāyāḥ paśūnāṃ bhavati ya evaṃ veda ||
english: The cloud is the fat; marrow is the final resting-place. He who knows thus becomes the foundation of prosperity, of offspring, and of cattle.

sanskrit: indraḥ prāṅ tiṣṭhan dakṣiṇā tiṣṭhan yamaḥ pratyaṅ tiṣṭhan dhātodaṅ tiṣṭhan savitā | tṛṇāni prāptaḥ somo rājāvṛtta ānandaḥ | īkṣamāno mitre yujyamāno vaiśvadevo yuktaḥ prajāpatir vimuktaḥ sarvam | etad vai gorūpam | upainaṃ rūpavantaḥ paśavas tiṣṭhanti ya evaṃ veda ||
english: Indra stands to the east; Yama stands to the south; Dhātṛ stands to the west; Savitṛ stands to the north. King Soma, having reached the grasses, is Ānanda turned away. Being seen, he is in Mitra; being yoked, he is Vaiśvadeva; when yoked, Prajāpati; when unyoked, the All. This is verily the form of the cow. Cattle possessed of fair form attend upon him who knows thus.
